newsitem.title: CANADA: SEC's Levitt urges update of securities regulation.
newsitem.headline: SEC's Levitt urges update of securities regulation.

text.p: Regulators should discard outdated rules and use modern technology to create effective supervision of global electronic trading, Arthur Levitt, chairman of the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission, said on Wednesday.
"We must work closely with the securities industry to provide a cost-effective system," he told the International Organisation of Securities Commissions convention.
The SEC's 1994 voluntary reporting agreement with six of the biggest U.S. securities firms covering over-the-counter derivatives trading is a model of how self-regulation can work, Levitt said.
Self-regulation may sometimes be deficient and then the regulator must step in and bring about chanage, he added.

"We must deal with today's problems with new tehmology to gain the insights we need into the new global trading patterns, but without stifling the world's most innovative industry," Levitt said. "We must ensure the highest standards of investor protection."
Bilateral agreements between national regulators are no longer enough, he said, and worldwide cooperation is needed.
